decision: The Gurvich 1996 evaluation represented by NASA is the scientifically preferred direction among the inspected choices: it revises both the thermal construction and the experimental energy analysis. Production coefficients remain unchanged in this scoped investigation; retaining them is not a claim that JANAF is scientifically superior.

identity.species: Neutral ideal-gas sodium hydroxide dimer (NaOH)2 = Na2(OH)2 = H2Na2O2 = NASA Na2O2H2; six atoms, twelve vibrational modes.
identity.excluded: Not Na2O2 peroxide, NaOH monomer, NaOH(H2O)n hydrate, hydroxide ions, or condensed NaOH. Formula equality alone would not establish a different cluster topology.
identity.state: Old C2h and revised D2h empirical molecular representations describe the same nominal dimer. Ground electronic statistical weight is 1 in both evaluations. No experimentally established complete high-temperature state inventory is claimed.

source_lineage.current: Unchanged FastChem H2Na2O2 row cites JANAF 1998. Official H-062 table retains a December 1970 evaluation date; 1998 is the compilation edition, not new dimer measurements. Current polynomial approximately follows the JANAF values at reviewed in-domain nodes.
source_lineage.janaf_construction: Inspected JANAF1974 p449 explains the adopted C2h model, twelve estimated vibrational frequencies, symmetry 2 and molecular inertia. Hf298=-145.2 +/-6.0 kcal/mol, equivalent central value -607.5168 kJ/mol. A mean gas dimerization H298=-50.7 +/-3.0 kcal/mol was combined with the adopted monomer energy. Original 1-atm/cal table is not used as a 1-bar Gibbs table.
source_lineage.revised_construction: Gurvich1996 pp1268-1271 prefers a D2h planar rhomboid by analogy, revises empirical vibrational frequencies and thermal functions in a rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator model with low-temperature quantum corrections, and reanalyzes previous vapor experiments using revised auxiliary data. NASA record explicitly cites Gurvich,1996b. and reproduces selected absolute Table3-27 functions.
source_lineage.shared_ancestry: JANAF and Gurvich reuse older vaporization, mass-spectrometric and molecular-beam studies. Neither their agreement nor NASA reproduction is independent experimental validation. Modern monomer-only spectroscopy would not establish the dimer partition function.

schoonmaker1958.inspection: Original full text not read; publisher request HTTP403, bibliographic metadata confirmed. Values below are as reported in Gurvich1996.

rao1960.inspection: Original full text not read; publisher request HTTP403, bibliographic metadata confirmed. Interpretation is Gurvich1996 evaluation.
rao1960.interpretation: Gurvich considers the monomer/dimer pressure ratio more reliable than absolute pressures because systematic errors can cancel. Condensed-phase composition and creeping molten hydroxide can affect vapor experiments.

formation_energy_evidence.gurvich_selected_reaction: NaOH(l) + NaOH(g) -> Na2(OH)2(g), with extrapolated reaction H0=-4.9 +/-6 kJ/mol; this is neither all-gas association nor total atomization D0.
formation_energy_evidence.uncertainty: Evaluated bounds are not identified as Gaussian one-sigma errors and share ancestral data. No probabilistic source-combination error bar is calculated.

geometry_evidence.reported_by_evaluations: Both inspected evaluations cite Buchler et al.1967 for nonpolarity and a planar Na2O2 fragment. Nonpolarity does not uniquely choose C2h versus D2h or locate H atoms.
geometry_evidence.original_access: Publisher title and Crossref abstract inspected, original full text not read. The title/abstract concern Cs-containing species and do not name NaOH. They do not establish whether the full text also discusses NaOH; no citation error is inferred.
geometry_evidence.high_temperature_limit: Gurvich explicitly uses estimated molecular constants and acknowledges increasing high-temperature approximation uncertainty. D2h is an evaluated assumption, not directly measured molecular geometry in this review.

numerical_interpretation.replay: Exact modern official JANAF dimer nodes reproduce the frozen comparison using frozen atomic references. Molecular energy, molecular thermal changes and atomic reference changes are separated.
numerical_interpretation.rrho: The twelve printed modes explain the Cp difference. Adding the classical rotor inertia/symmetry entropy difference also reproduces the entropy change, within printed precision/approximation. This diagnostic does not recompute a validated high-temperature partition function.
numerical_interpretation.association: 2NaOH(g)->dimer uses each source own monomer. Atomic references cancel, but switching both monomer and dimer is a different comparison from replacing only the dimer.
numerical_interpretation.printed_inconsistencies: Gurvich Table3-24 reports a 1000K entropy difference of15.049 J/mol/K whereas its absolute Table3-27 and official JANAF imply19.052. The absolute table is reproduced by NASA and the RRHO diagnostic. Both printed values are preserved. The inertia-product uncertainty is also5000 in prose and500 in the list, with units1e-117 g^3 cm^6; neither is silently corrected or propagated.

follow_ups.action: Construct a named candidate replacing only the dimer with the reviewed Gurvich/NASA thermal and energy source, using explicit common atomic references. Check thermodynamic consistency and a focused fixed-network substitution before adoption; keep a monomer+dimer update as a separate model choice.

Inspect Rao1960 and Schoonmaker1958 originals to audit pressure ratios, species assignment, condensed-phase conditions and third-law recalculation; verify whether Buchler1967 discusses NaOH in the full text. These remain source-audit gaps, not blockers for merging the completed investigation.

If cooler sodium-rich or high-pressure applications make the dimer important, seek independent molecular constants, low-mode anharmonicity and quantified state/structural uncertainty rather than extrapolating the finite-grid result. No exhaustive negative literature claim is made.
